author: time news
title: The Sweet Deception: Aspartame and the Need for Informed Choices
text:
• Dr. Jimmy Mohamed, a prominent French physician, raised concerns about aspartame, an artificial sweetener.
• Aspartame is composed of aspartic acid and phenylalanine, and is approximately 200 times sweeter than sugar.
• It is commonly found in diet sodas, sugar-free desserts, and various processed foods.
• Research on aspartame's long-term health effects remains inconclusive.
• Some studies suggest potential links between aspartame consumption and health issues, including neurological effects, cancer risk, and metabolic disorders.
• The International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) classifies aspartame as 'possibly carcinogenic to humans'.
• The Joint Expert Committee on Food Additives (JECFA) states that current evidence does not support a causal link between aspartame and cancer.
• Dr. Mohamed emphasizes the importance of critically evaluating data on food additives.
• He advises consumers to read food labels, choose whole foods, limit processed foods, stay informed, and consult with healthcare professionals.
• The FDA considers aspartame safe within acceptable daily intake limits but acknowledges potential adverse effects for some individuals.
• Ongoing research may lead to stricter regulations or a shift towards alternative sweeteners.
